skills.name: State the uses of sulphur and its compounds

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to list the main uses of sulphur, sulphur dioxide and sulphuric acid, and say which property each use depends on.
Builds on: Lessons {2} to {8}, which give the properties behind each use.
Leads to: the nitrogen chapter, where fertilisers made with sulphuric acid appear again.

sections.heading: Sulphur and sulphur dioxide
Sulphuric acid

key_words.meaning: heating rubber with sulphur to link its chains
a substance that kills fungi such as mildew
a liquid that conducts electricity by its ions
cleaning a metal surface with acid before plating

examples: sulphur → sulphuric acid: the largest use

mistake.wrong: sulphur dioxide is used in car batteries
mistake.right: dilute sulphuric acid is used in car batteries
mistake.why: The battery needs an electrolyte, which is the acid, not the gas.

worked_example.problem: Give three uses of sulphuric acid, with the industry for each.
steps: Fertiliser: ammonia is neutralised with the acid to give ammonium sulphate.
Batteries: dilute sulphuric acid is the electrolyte of a lead-acid car battery.
Metals: the acid pickles steel, cleaning the surface before it is plated.
Others include detergents, paints, dyes, plastics and refining petroleum.
worked_example.answer: fertilisers, car batteries and pickling steel (among many others)

cards.idea: The largest use of sulphur is making sulphuric acid.
Sulphur vulcanises rubber, making tyres harder and more elastic.
example: the sulphur links the rubber chains together

check.prompt: Match each substance to a use.

pool.right: The electrolyte of a car battery

cards.idea: {formula('SO2')} preserves food and bleaches delicate materials.
example: dried fruit and fruit juice are treated with it

pick.y: A little {formula('SO2')} kills the bacteria and moulds that spoil the juice.

pick.q: as the liquid inside a car battery
pick.y: A lead-acid battery uses dilute sulphuric acid as its electrolyte.

pick.q: to make tyres harder and more elastic
pick.y: Heating rubber with sulphur links its chains: this is vulcanising.

pick.q: to make the fertiliser ammonium sulphate
pick.y: Ammonia is neutralised with sulphuric acid to give {formula('(NH4)2SO4')}.

pick.q: What is the largest single use of sulphur?
e: Matches use only a small amount of sulphur.
Vulcanising is important but uses far less sulphur than the acid industry.
Fungicides use a small amount compared with the acid industry.
pick.y: Most mined sulphur is burned to {formula('SO2')} and turned into sulphuric acid by the Contact process.

pick.q: Why is sulphur added to rubber?
pick.r: To vulcanise it, making it harder and more elastic
w: To make it burn more easily
To make it dissolve in water
e: Rubber is not treated with sulphur in order to burn it.
Vulcanised rubber is not yellow; the change is in its strength, not its colour.
Rubber does not dissolve in water either before or after.
pick.y: Sulphur links the rubber chains together, so the rubber keeps its shape and wears better in tyres.

pick.q: Which use depends on sulphur dioxide being a preservative?
pick.r: Treating dried fruit and fruit juice so that they keep
e: A car battery uses sulphuric ACID, not the gas as a preservative.
Fertiliser is made with sulphuric acid, not with the gas as a preservative.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} kills bacteria and moulds, so it is used in small amounts to preserve food and drink.

pick.q: Which of these is made using sulphuric acid?
e: Salt is obtained by evaporating sea water; no acid is needed.
Limestone is quarried, not made with acid.
Charcoal is made by heating wood out of contact with air.
pick.y: Ammonia is neutralised with sulphuric acid to give {formula('(NH4)2SO4')}, a widely used fertiliser.

pick.q: Why is sulphuric acid used in a car battery?
pick.r: It is the electrolyte that lets the battery give a current
w: It stops the battery from rusting
e: Rusting is not what the acid is there to prevent.
Cooling is not its purpose; batteries are cooled by air.
The acid does not act as a cleaner; it carries the current as ions.
pick.y: A lead-acid battery uses dilute sulphuric acid as its electrolyte.

pick.q: Which use of sulphur depends on its killing fungi?
pick.r: Dusting crops to control mildew and other fungal diseases
e: Gunpowder uses sulphur because it burns, not because it kills fungi.
Matches use sulphur because it catches fire easily.
Making the acid depends on burning the sulphur.
pick.y: Sulphur dust and lime-sulphur sprays are used as fungicides on crops.

questions.prompt: What mass of sulphuric acid, in grams, is needed to make {n} mol of ammonium sulphate, {formula('(NH4)2SO4')}?

misconceptions.explain: The question asks for the mass of the ACID, not of the fertiliser.
{1} mol of acid is needed for {1} mol of ammonium sulphate, not {2}.

solution: {2}{formula('NH3')} + {formula('H2SO4')} → {formula('(NH4)2SO4')}: {1} mol of acid gives {1} mol of the fertiliser.
The relative molecular mass of {formula('H2SO4')} is {molarMass('H2SO4')}.

pick.r: It is used at some stage in a very wide range of industries, from fertilisers to metals and plastics
pick.w1: It is the most expensive chemical made
pick.w2: It is used only in the making of fertilisers
pick.w3: It is the only acid that can be made in a factory
pick.y: Because so many different industries need it, its use rises with industry as a whole.

pick.r: Fertilisers, detergents, paints, dyes, plastics, batteries and metal treatment all need it
pick.w1: It is used only in car batteries
pick.w2: It is the cheapest chemical to transport
pick.w3: It cannot be imported, so every country must make its own
pick.y: A long list of industries depend on it, so its use follows the size of the whole industrial base.

pick.r: Its use grows with the number of factories, not with the size of the population
pick.w1: Its use grows with the population only
pick.w2: Its use is fixed by law in every country
pick.w3: It is used mainly in homes rather than in factories
pick.y: It is an industrial chemical, so its use measures industry rather than the number of people.
